 Video Extensometer 
 Video extensometer
The video extensometer ONE1 is a non-contact deformation measuring device for material testing on the basis of high-resolution video technology using the surface structure or, if required, markings.
The video extensometer is used for the optical measurement of length change and is suitable for tensile tests, compression tests, bending tests and torsion tests on all materials.
 Video extensometer ONE1 for material testing
Advantages 
Suitable for tensile, compression, bending, shear and torsion tests on all materials 
Non-contact measuring method 
With a suitable surface structure, no artificial marking is required 
Easy handling 
Robust housing for use in laboratory and industrial environments 
Indirect measurement via mirror possible 
Reliably applicable for different specimen thicknesses without modification or recalibration up to ±15 mm 
Insensitive to interference due to the use of blue light in a small wavelength range and polarization filters 
Stable and reproducible; class 0.5 according to ISO 9513 in the mentioned field of view 
Can be used for strain measurement and strain control 
Can be used in combination with temperature chambers and high temperature furnaces up to 1400°C (without additional costs) 
Easily expandable for combined determination of longitudinal and lateral strain or as a multi-camera system for larger fields of view 
Automatic determination of the strain characteristics based on the defined initial gauge length and the range of maximum strain 
Simultaneous evaluation of several strain ranges 
Segmented evaluation of the complete free length (strain distribution possible) - advantage: specimen break always in the strain measurement range 
Evaluation of different initial measuring lengths 
 Options for the video extensometer
 Multi-camera system
Depending on requirements, several video extensometers can be combined.
Variant 1 - "Splitted mode"
Very large samples can be analyzed using two cameras (one camera per measuring mark).
Variant 2 - Measurement of different parameters
One camera with a high-resolution measuring range for evaluating elastic deformation and another camera with a large field of view for evaluating elongation at break
 DIC Module (Digital Image Correlation)
Video measurement technology for deformation measurement and image evaluation using digital image correlation (DIC) for spatially resolved strain analysis to create 2D deformation maps 
Determination of local strains (spatially and directionally resolved) 
Creation of color-coded area maps (can be recorded as individual images and as videos to visualize the strain distribution) 
Illustration and evaluation of complex changes in components during testing 
Enables post-process analysis, e.g., of carbon fiber reinforced composites 
Surface measurement for calculating strain and displacement maps

 Optical 3D measuring system
Advantages and applications for deformation measurement using 3D measuring principle: 
Integrated system: Deformation data (e.g. tensile elongation) is transferred directly to the testing software and analysed
 → Multiple deformation channels can be used for integrated analysis 
Increased measuring accuracy for longitudinal and transverse strain measurement by correcting the movement of the test specimen in the Z direction (out-of-plane movement) 
→ Reduction of measurement errors due to clamping or alignment effects 
Optical deformation measurement for tensile/compression or component tests in the X, Y, and Z axes  
Variable 3D deformation evaluation including time-synchronous force measurement values with the option of DIC and post-processing (3D measurement maps with regional deformation ratios)
